page: Microsoft Azure D32ps_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dpsv6 server family, operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is built on the arm64 architecture, featuring a Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor with 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The system allocates 128.0 GB of memory, resulting in a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no integrated local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance, though it is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

In benchmark evaluations, the D32ps_v6 demonstrates strong multi-core performance and memory efficiency. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test and Geekbench multi-core score both rank in the top 25%, reflecting the efficiency of its 32 dedicated physical cores. Memory performance is a notable strength, with large-block read and write memory bandwidth, as well as the Passmark memory score, placing in the top 10% tier. Database operations measured via Passmark also rank in the top 10% tier. Conversely, single-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench remains in the average middle 50% range. Large-scale LLM inference, such as prompt processing on a 70B model, represents a performance tradeoff, ranking in the bottom 10%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D32ps_v6 offers a high-density resource profile by utilizing ARM-based architecture to deliver 32 dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading. This design provides predictable compute performance per resource. Given its strong multi-threaded decompression, software compilation, and database operation benchmarks, this server is suited for multi-threaded workloads, web serving, software development pipelines, and database operations that leverage its high memory bandwidth.
